title: Binance driving USD1 adoption
summary: Binance listed USD1 early (2025-05-22, after HTX, MEXC and KuCoin) and ran a capped, month-long promotion of up to 20% APR that WLF reportedly helped fund. Independent data put about 85-87% of USD1 on Binance. WLF calls the incentives standard practice, and it did post a $159.5M annualized USD1 revenue run rate in April 2026. The specific WSJ chart tying every usage jump to Binance could not be accessed, but Bloomberg and Forbes analyses support the underlying point.

sub_claims.statement: Binance was one of the first exchanges to list USD1 for trading.
sub_claims.finding: Binance opened USD1/USDT spot trading on 2025-05-22 with no listing fee, after HTX, MEXC and KuCoin (2025-05-21). That makes it 'one of the first', but not the first.

sub_claims.statement: Binance effectively paid customers ~20% annual yield to hold USD1.
sub_claims.finding: A Binance 'booster' promotion paid up to 20% APR on flexible USD1 Earn products from about 2025-12-24 to 2026-01-23, with bonus tiers reportedly capped at about 50,000 USD1 per user. Market cap rose from about $2.74B to $2.89B. A $40M reward pool followed on 2026-01-22. A person familiar told Bloomberg that WLF provides a marketing budget for these promotions. The 20% was a temporary, capped rate, not a standing yield.

sub_claims.statement: A WSJ chart showed each major jump in USD1 usage was linked to Binance.
sub_claims.finding: The WSJ article could not be accessed. The supporting evidence: supply jumped from about $130M to $2.1B with the MGX-Binance $2B deal (May 2025) and later grew with Binance listings and promotions; about 85-87% of USD1 sits on Binance (Arkham, Nansen, Kaiko; Forbes: $4.7B of $5.4B on 2026-02-09); Bloomberg attributes WLF's stablecoin profits partly to the Binance promotional arrangement. Arkham later put Binance's custody share at about 89%.

sub_claims.statement: World Liberty says this is standard industry practice for marketing a stablecoin.
sub_claims.finding: A WLF spokesman called the funded incentives 'standard practice' for stablecoin issuers and denied that Binance has any control over WLF. Binance denies giving preferential treatment.

sub_claims.statement: WLF brags it makes ~$159M annually from USD1, 'compounding, accelerating'.
sub_claims.finding: In April 2026 WLF posted a $159.5M annualized USD1 revenue 'run rate'. That is a run rate, not booked annual revenue. Bloomberg estimated nearly $150M for 2026. The 'compounding, accelerating' wording was not independently confirmed. Later context: Cointelegraph (2026-10-19, CoinGecko data) reported USD1 supply fell about $401M (9.1%) from 2026-10-06, driven by redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain, with reserves of about $4.01B. A smaller base implies a lower run rate, which cuts against 'compounding, accelerating'.

sub_claims.statement: USD1 revenue flows to WLF, which pays the president and his family.
sub_claims.finding: Bloomberg values WLF's stablecoin business at about $1.7B, with the Trump family's stake at about $630M. The exact split of USD1 income is not public.

corrections: Transcript implies Binance was among the very first to list USD1; HTX, MEXC and KuCoin listed it before Binance's 2025-05-22 listing.
Transcript says customers were paid 20% annual yield; the record shows a capped (~50,000 USD1/user per reports), roughly one-month promotional APR of 'up to' 20% (Dec 2025-Jan 2026).
Transcript says WLF makes $159M annually; WLF's April 2026 figure was a $159.5M annualized run rate, not realized annual revenue.
The WSJ chart could not be independently accessed; comparable Bloomberg (2026-06-05) and Forbes (2026-02-09) analyses support the Binance-concentration point.
denials_and_context: WLF: incentives are standard practice for stablecoin issuers and are funded by WLF; Binance has no control over WLF; WLF runs promotions on other exchanges too.

Binance: 'has not provided preferential treatment to World Liberty Financial'; hosts more than 15 stablecoins and promotes others; no revenue sharing with WLF. CEO Richard Teng denied boosting WLF ahead of the CZ pardon.
It is unclear how much of the USD1 held at Binance belongs to the exchange and how much to its customers.
The link to the CZ pardon is inference by critics (e.g., Sens. Warren and Merkley); no documented quid pro quo.
